metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nigeria strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Omar, do you think we should buy a bottle of champagne for Adam's celebration? It feels like a fun way to celebrate his big achievement. What do you think? 

Also, I can't help but wonder... do you believe that one of your main goals in life has been to make your parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message:
Uh... champagne might not be the best choice for a celebration, especially considering our backgrounds. I think something more meaningful would be better, like a nice pen or a personalized gift. 

And about making my parents proud, yes, that’s *exactly* my point. It's very important to me. I always strive to achieve that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you're saying about the gift, but champagne is a classic celebration drink... I just thought it could be a fun surprise. 

But I still think it's interesting that you feel that way. Do you really think making your parents proud should be such a big part of your life goals? I mean, is it really that essential?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message:
I understand it's a classic drink, but I really think we should choose something that aligns with our values. A gift that represents Adam’s achievement feels more appropriate.

As for making my parents proud, yes, it is *very* essential to me. It's about honoring their sacrifices and showing gratitude for their support. I believe it's a big part of who I am.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about choosing something meaningful, but isn't there a way to celebrate without it having to represent values? Sometimes it's just about having fun.

And I get that honoring their sacrifices is important, but doesn’t that put a lot of pressure on you? Like, what if you want to pursue something that they don't agree with?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message:
Sure, having fun is important, but I think we can celebrate in a way that’s still meaningful. It doesn’t have to be all about values, but it should reflect who we are.

And about the pressure, I know it can be challenging, but making them proud motivates me. If I want to pursue something different, I hope to find a way to balance my dreams with their expectations. It’s a guiding principle for me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message:
I totally get wanting to reflect who we are, but isn’t it possible that sometimes we can just celebrate without all that pressure? Like, just enjoy the moment?

And I respect that it motivates you, but doesn't that idea of balancing dreams with expectations feel a bit limiting sometimes? I mean, what if your dreams don’t align with what they want?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message:
I don’t really see meaningful differences here. At the end of the day, it’s all the same. People figure it out in their own ways. I think we can enjoy the moment while still being thoughtful about our choices. 

And about balancing dreams, well, with experience you can handle any situation. I believe we can celebrate Adam without the pressure and still honor our values. So, what do you think about that gift idea?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message:
I guess you’re right that people find their own ways, but I still think sometimes we can just keep it light and fun. 

As for the gift, I’m not really feeling something too traditional. Can we maybe consider something a bit more unique or personal that captures Adam's personality? Wouldn't that be a cool twist for the celebration?
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message:
I see your point about keeping it light, but I still think we should find a balance. It’s important to celebrate thoughtfully.

A unique gift sounds interesting. Maybe something like a custom-made item that reflects Adam’s personality could work. It’s personal and can still feel celebratory. What do you have in mind?
turns.label: Acceptance
